Last visit i went to, the appointments were running late so the team adjusted and sent out the tech to us to talk to us while the vet was busy. very nice of them to do that ^^ I usually recommend this place off of the service alone

I am very disappointed with the way we and our cat were treated at this clinic.

Yesterday, we brought our cat Chan to the clinic because he was having serious problems urinating. He had X-rays, urine tests, a catheter was placed, and we were told that everything was fine: his temperature was normal, there were no kidney stones, and there was no blood. We were told that he would receive treatment to clear the urinary tract, that he was doing well, eating normally, and that we would be able to take him home in the morning.

The cost was already very high — approximately $2,500 — but, of course, our main concern was our cat's health.

The next morning, another doctor told us that they had found some crystals and that he wanted to check something else. We asked whether we could take Chan home if everything was okay, and we were told that they would call us back. Nobody called.

We came to the clinic at 10:00 a.m. and were told that Chan was not ready and that the doctor was not there. We were asked to wait for a call at 2:30 p.m. Again, nobody called. We returned at 3:00 p.m. and were told that the doctor was still unavailable and that only a technician could speak with us.

We waited for about an hour because we wanted to see our cat and, most importantly, speak to the doctor about his condition. Unfortunately, the doctor could not find even five minutes to come out and explain what was happening with our pet.

Instead, the technician gave us Chan's medications and a handwritten note with instructions from the doctor. That was the end of our visit.

The final bill was approximately $3,000.

I understand that veterinary medicine can be expensive, and I am willing to pay for necessary treatment when it is for the health of my pet. What I find unacceptable is the lack of communication and the lack of respect shown to us as clients. When you are leaving your beloved pet at a clinic and paying thousands of dollars, you expect clear information, communication, and at least a few minutes of the doctor's time to explain your pet's condition and treatment.

Our biggest concern was never the money — it was Chan. We simply wanted to know how he was doing and to understand what had been done to him and what we needed to do after bringing him home.

I sincerely hope the clinic will improve its communication with pet owners and show more consideration for both the animals in their care and the people who are worried about them.
Great team, good price, and I'll be back in the future!

I’m really disappointed with my experience at Royal Vet. We’ve been clients there for a while, and I found the consultations to be fairly affordable. So, whenever there was any doubt, it was easy to find out what was going on with your cat or dog.

I went there last Monday because my cat had a urinary blockage. It wasn’t the first time he had gotten blocked. The last time it happened at my other vet, it cost me around $500–700. At Royal Vet, they gave me a $3,600 treatment plan. I had to go through it and remove certain things because I found what they wanted to do excessive. In the end, it cost me $1,300 just to get him unblocked, which is basically double what my other vet charged me.

I also asked them to neuter my other cat once the procedure was finished. They gave me an estimate of $550 + tax. Nothing else was included, just the neutering. I found that price ridiculous. So I called my previous vet and, strangely enough, they charge me $320 for the consultation AND the neutering.

That’s when I realized I had basically gotten ripped off for the urinary blockage treatment.

Avoid this place. It’s a cash grab.

In English:
I want to share my experience with this veterinary clinic because I am deeply disappointed. We needed an evaluation for our perfectly healthy, 4-year-old English bulldog for an upcoming international trip, as we are moving. The vet (who works for the director) confirmed a perfect heart during the check-up. However, she then decided to make our dog run for 3 minutes in 35-degree heat on the scorching asphalt. I had to insist that they put him on the grass as a precaution. Meanwhile, the director walked by with her own bulldog, which was even bigger. After we spoke with the vet, everything seemed fine, but after this discussion, she suggested postponing the trip for several months. I therefore question the motivation behind this postponement, as there was no valid reason. Furthermore, the service was extremely slow, and despite the refusal to issue the certificate, we had to pay nearly $300. If this clinic were truly committed to the well-being of brachycephalic breeds, they would ensure that airlines allow these dogs in the cabin, not at exorbitant cargo costs. To me, this is no longer about animal welfare, but about profit. I leave this clinic with a feeling of injustice, and I absolutely cannot recommend it.
